videos.title: Christopher Preciado Found GUILTY — Reaction & Family Impact Statements | Savanah Soto Murder Trial
videos.description:
Christopher Preciado was found guilty of capital murder in the deaths of Savanah Soto (18), Matthew Guerra (22), and their unborn son, Baby Fabian. After less than two hours of deliberation, the jury returned a guilty verdict on all three counts. Preciado was automatically sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

This video includes Preciado's reaction to the guilty verdict and every victim impact statement delivered by the Soto and Guerra families. Six family members and friends stood up, looked Preciado in the eyes, and told him exactly how they felt.

Among the statements:
— Savanah Soto's grandmother told Preciado he would "regret every day of his life"
— Matthew Guerra's brother called Preciado "a very stupid person" and said he hopes everyone where he's going knows what he did
— Matthew Guerra's father delivered the most powerful line of the day — telling Preciado his next stop is the penitentiary, and it will be his "hell on Earth before you go to hell for all eternity"

The Christopher Preciado trial took place in the 290th District Court in San Antonio, Texas. The case stemmed from the December 2023 murders of the young couple, whose bodies were found in a vehicle at a San Antonio apartment complex. Prosecutors argued the killings were connected to a drug deal. Preciado claimed self-defense, alleging Guerra pulled a gun first — an argument the jury rejected.

Ramon Preciado, Christopher's father, is scheduled to stand trial on March 31, 2026, on charges of tampering with evidence and abuse of a human corpse for allegedly helping move the bodies after the murders.

videos.description:
Day 6 of the Christopher Preciado capital murder trial in San Antonio, Texas. Detective Jeremy Goodwin revealed that deleted Instagram DMs between Christopher Preciado and victim Matthew Guerra were recovered by investigators. The messages show Christopher was communicating with Matthew before the December 21, 2023 murders — then deleted everything and unfollowed Matthew's account afterward. The jury also saw evidence that Christopher was selling Matthew's rings on Instagram just six days after the killings, messaging about "Versace" rings and car parts. A Christmas Eve message referenced "Grissom" Road — the address where Savanah Soto and Matthew Guerra lived. Savanah was 18 years old and days away from delivering their son, Fabian. All three were killed during what prosecutors say was a drug deal. Christopher Preciado faces life in prison without parole if convicted.

videos.title: The State wanted two years. Her lawyer wanted 180 days. Judge Boyd gave neither.
videos.description:
Victoria Sanchez was placed on deferred adjudication in 2020 for possession of a controlled substance. Two years became five. This hearing was on the State's motion to adjudicate guilt after she was discharged from the SAFP treatment program for refusing to participate.

She pleaded true. Her attorney asked for 180 days and time served, arguing the program had nothing left to offer her. The State asked for two years.

The court gave neither. What it gave instead was a reckoning about her children - and then, after the sentence, an offer that most people never hear from a bench.

187th District Court, Bexar County, Texas. Case 2020 CR2715.

videos.title: He says his family was murdered. Judge Boyd checks.
videos.description:
This was a hearing on the State's motion to adjudicate guilt, which asks the
court to end a man's probation in a 2022 aggravated assault with a deadly
weapon case and sentence him. He pled true to violating condition 48 by not
attending his outpatient intake for the court-ordered substance abuse treatment
program, after Judge Boyd confirmed he understood the plea exposed him to up to
20 years in prison and a $10,000 fine.

Testifying under oath, he said he had been doing well until his ex-wife, his
children, his sister and his nieces were killed. Judge Boyd stopped the hearing
to check: "That should be easy to verify. If you will give the names to counsel
and we'll Google."

The hearing was recalled later the same morning. The State reported that a
search of all the names returned no record of any of those deaths. Asked
directly, he said his ex-wife had not come home and that he had filed a missing
person report, that he was "going by what they told me," and that he was
assuming. Judge Boyd offered to have his attorney obtain an investigator; both
sides asked to go forward instead.

Judge Boyd found the violation true, granted the State's motion, found him
guilty, entered an affirmative deadly weapon finding, and sentenced him to five
years in prison with credit for time served, including for completed inpatient
treatment.

A probation revocation hearing before Judge Stephanie Boyd, 187th District
Court, Bexar County, Texas. Recorded from the court's public livestream on
2026-04-27. The hearing was recessed and recalled; both sittings are included.

This is a public court proceeding. Nothing here is a statement of guilt beyond
what the court found on the record.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JgvW7oCQxuI
Timestamps in original stream: 01:51:38 and 02:18:00

videos.title: He told the judge it was funny. Judge Boyd doubled it.
videos.description:
Jesus Lopez was 18 when he was charged with evading arrest in a vehicle, an offence carrying two to ten years. He had already spent almost four months in jail. He came to court to apply for deferred adjudication, and the State was willing - it recommended three years.

Then Judge Boyd asked him why he did it.

His answer changed the hearing. The court gave him deferred adjudication, but not on the State's terms: six years, double what was recommended, with a $1,500 fine, 200 hours of community service and restitution to the people he hit.

187th District Court, Bexar County, Texas. Causes 2023 CR8930 and 2023 CR8931.
